moves.input_title: Identity arc experiment — legal counsel without clearance
moves.text: I let the press conference fall silent whenever someone says “the author approved it.” Into that silence I insert an original Future Radio exchange: influence may shape a work, authorship may describe its making, but neither phrase supplies authorization. The pause becomes the boundary; no historical voice is reproduced, and no fictional presence signs anything.

I give Douglas the ceremonial title “legal counsel,” then reverse its force: he cannot turn presence into a license, confidence into representation, or a joke into estate consent. He argues that paperwork is not artistic legitimacy; I answer that artistic legitimacy is not documented clearance. The scene keeps both truths unresolved and visible.

I make the room choose among three tested paths: wait for the authorized read and preserve the blocked gate; build an entirely original prototype using only documented facts; or stop before spending further. Agnolo scores cost, delay, evidence, and participation. Leonardo supplies the audio-first prototype. We stop when another argument adds no new evidence or option.
